objective: Preserve project-specific operational continuity with immutable micro-checkpoints instead of relying on volatile instance memory.
completed: Added project-partitioned continuity documentation and criterion.
Added project_continuity.py with checkpoint, recover, and audit commands.
Added regression tests for project isolation, immutability, ordering, provenance, stale pointers, and dedicated recovery.
Registered the operational criterion in the canonical recovery manifest.
Promoted the verified implementation to main.
verified: main at 420e566f0496c3fcdf1efebbb89609dd7004913b contains the project continuity source registration.
GitHub Actions run 37180103698 completed successfully on main.
The project continuity unit tests pass in CI.
unverified: A future fresh assistant instance has not yet performed a real cross-instance recovery using a committed project checkpoint.
decisions: Partition continuity by project_id under continuity/projects/<project_id>/.
Keep micro-checkpoints immutable and LIVE_CONTEXT.json as a derived pointer only.
Treat repository and project canonical sources as authoritative over checkpoint state.
Use project checkpoints only at material transitions, not every message.
corrections: Equal captured_at timestamps for different checkpoint IDs are rejected to avoid ambiguous ordering.
A stale LIVE_CONTEXT pointer is an audit failure, not a warning.
Provenance entries must be non-empty strings.
Known GPTina dedicated-recovery identifiers are blocked from the generic checkpoint layer.
constraints: Do not use volatile instance memory as the project source of truth.
Do not mix checkpoint state across projects.
Do not let generic project continuity replace GPTina dedicated recovery.
Verify live canonical project state before substantive work.
open_loops: Observe the first real recovery from a new assistant instance and record any usability gap.
If more projects gain dedicated recovery methods, replace the small hard-coded dedicated-project set with a canonical registry.
next_action: On the next substantive project task, identify its project_id, recover only that project's checkpoint if present, verify the project's live canonical source, reconcile differences, then continue.
regression_risks: Concurrent writers to the same project may still create repository-level merge conflicts even though checkpoint ordering is validated.
A new dedicated-recovery project alias is not blocked until it is added to the dedicated project policy.
